column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah,

establish the prayer and give the zakāh. If they do that, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with Allah the Exalted.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
Umirtu (“I have been commanded”): my Lord has commanded me, since none commands the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
An uqātila (“to fight”): that is, bi-an uqātila; omitting the preposition before an is common.

Al-nās (“the people”): the idolaters other than the People of the Book, because of the narration of al-Nasāʾī: “I have been commanded to fight the idolaters until they testify that there is no god but Allah.” The meaning of this statement is made clear by the narration of Muslim from Ṭāriq: “Whoever affirms the oneness of Allah and disbelieves in what is worshipped besides Allah, his wealth and his blood become inviolable.”
“Establish the prayer”: keep performing it constantly, with its conditions.
What is meant by prayer here is the obligatory prayer, not prayer in general.
“Give the zakāh”: give the obligatory zakāh to those entitled to it.

“If they do that”: the word “do” is used here for something partly consisting of words, by way of giving the majority precedence, or intending the more general sense, since speech is an action of the tongue.
ʿAṣamū (“they have protected”): they have safeguarded and preserved.

“Except by the right of Islam”: if something comes from them for which the ruling of Islam requires them to be held to account, such as retaliation, a prescribed punishment, compensation for damage, or the like.
“And their reckoning”: for what is in their hearts,

“is with Allah”: since He alone knows what is in the hearts, whether disbelief, hypocrisy or anything else. Whoever is sincere in his faith, He rewards him with the reward of the sincere; and whoever is not, the rulings of the Muslims are applied to him in this world and he is punished in the Hereafter.
Uttering the two testimonies is a condition for being judged a Muslim.

Fighting the idolaters is not halted except when they utter the two testimonies; as for the People of the Book, they are fought until one of two ends: Islam or paying the jizyah, according to the texts that indicate this.
Fighting those who abandon the prayer and the zakāh.
Islam protects blood and wealth, and likewise honour, [as in] the hadith: “Your blood, your wealth and your honour are inviolable to you…”, to the end of the hadith.
Rulings are applied only according to outward appearances, and Allah takes charge of what is hidden.

It is not obligatory to learn the proofs of the theologians and to know Allah through them, for the Prophet ﷺ was satisfied with what is mentioned in the hadith and did not stipulate knowledge of theological proofs. The many mutually supporting texts showing that this is not a condition together reach the level of mass transmission and certain knowledge.

Whoever utters the two testimonies, establishes the prayer and gives the zakāh is still held to account for the rights of Islam, such as retaliation, a prescribed punishment, compensation for damage and the like.
